headline: Senate resolution to cancel a 2025 federal rule changing Affordable Care Act marketplace enrollment rules did not advance.
what_it_does: This resolution would have used the Congressional Review Act to cancel a rule issued by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services on June 25, 2025. That rule shortened open enrollment on all health insurance exchanges to run from November 1 to December 31. It also required exchanges to check eligibility before enrollment for at least 75% of new special enrollment period sign-ups, and barred DACA recipients from exchange plans and state Basic Health Programs. The rule also stopped individual and small group insurers from covering certain sex-trait modification procedures as an essential health benefit, and the resolution would have undone all of these changes.

who_it_affects.group: People who buy health insurance on their own through ACA exchanges
who_it_affects.how: The resolution would have removed the rule's shorter open enrollment window and its stricter eligibility checks for special enrollment periods.
The resolution would have removed the rule's ban on DACA recipients enrolling in exchange plans or state Basic Health Programs.

who_it_affects.group: Low-income residents in states with Basic Health Programs
who_it_affects.how: The resolution would have reversed the rule's eligibility limits on these state programs for DACA recipients.

who_it_affects.group: Individual and small group health insurers
who_it_affects.how: The resolution would have removed the rule's ban on covering certain sex-trait modification procedures as an essential health benefit.
The resolution would have freed exchanges from the rule's required open enrollment dates and pre-enrollment verification requirements.
